name: Early Christian Necropolis of Pécs (Sopianae)
description: Beneath the streets of Pécs in southern Hungary lie the burial chambers of Sopianae, a Roman provincial town. Built in the 4th century, each tomb had an underground vault with a small chapel above ground. Inside, vivid murals show Christian scenes, making this one of the finest Roman cemeteries outside Italy and a rare glimpse of early Christian art.
